title: Bay services.yml
description: Schema for the Bay framework services.yml configuration file.

services.description: Service definitions — containers with Traefik routing and SSL.

^_.description: Reserved scratch keys (e.g. _anchors) for YAML anchor declarations. Ignored by the framework.

regions.description: Region restriction. Empty or absent means all regions.

depends_on.description: Service/accessory names this service depends on.

healthcheck_path.description: Path probed by `bin/bay healthcheck`. Use a route that exercises the dynamic backend (e.g. `/healthcheck`) when nginx and the app share a container — probing `/` would return nginx's static response even if the app process is dead.

config_files.description: Config files to copy into the stack directory.

public_routes.description: Routes exempt from VPN restriction (for vpn-access services).

vpn_routes.description: Routes protected by VPN on an otherwise public service.

zero_downtime.description: Enable canary zero-downtime deploy. Default false (opt-in).

health_check_timeout.description: How long this service may take to become healthy after a restart, in seconds. Two consumers: (1) rebuild.sh's post-restart health poll, which decides when to roll back — must be >= healthcheck.start_period, and has no effect if no healthcheck block is configured; (2) the post-deploy `bay healthcheck` URL probe's readiness window, where it can only widen the 90s framework default (a smaller value is ignored so the probe never gets stricter than baseline). Overrides git_deploy_health_check_timeout for this service. Default: 90 (group_vars) or framework default.

port.description: Host port binding. Prefer declaring the IP via `expose:` (loopback | tailnet | host) so the bind IP lives alongside the accessory. When both are set, `expose:` wins and any IP prefix in `port:` is replaced.

expose.description: Which host interface the accessory's port binds to. `loopback` (default) = 127.0.0.1; `gateway` = the active access gateway's overlay IP (`gateway_bind_ip`; deploy fails if the backend provides none). `tailnet` is a permanently-supported synonym for `gateway`, kept so existing services.yml files never need editing; `host` = 0.0.0.0 (explicit external exposure — unusual, expect reviewer friction).

expose_host_ack.description: Required acknowledgement for `expose: host`. A host-published port is DNAT'd in PREROUTING and never reaches the nftables `input` chain, so it is never seen by the CrowdSec bouncer. `bin/bay validate` fails on `expose: host` unless this flag is true. Setting it changes nothing about the rendered port binding — it records a reviewed acceptance of the bypass.

health_check_timeout.description: Rebuild.sh post-restart health poll timeout in seconds. Must be >= healthcheck.start_period. Has no effect if no healthcheck block is configured. Overrides git_deploy_health_check_timeout for this service. Default: 90 (group_vars) or framework default.

strategy.description: Build strategy: local (build on server), remote (build on build server, push to registry, server pulls), or registry (pull pre-built image from external CI). 'push' is a deprecated alias for 'remote'. Defaults to git_deploy_build_strategy.

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile path relative to repo root.

context.description: Build context path relative to repo root.

secrets.description: Build secrets — name to vault key mapping.

token.description: Vault key for git access token (private repos).

exclude.description: Gitignore-style glob patterns. Skip rebuild if ALL changed files match.

include.description: Reserved for future use. Not yet supported.

expose.description: Which host interface the service's internal port binds to. Optional — by default Traefik-fronted services have no host binding (reachable only inside the docker network). `loopback` = 127.0.0.1; `gateway` = the active access gateway's overlay IP (`gateway_bind_ip`; deploy fails if the backend provides none). `tailnet` is a permanently-supported synonym for `gateway`, kept so existing services.yml files never need editing; `host` = 0.0.0.0 (explicit external exposure — bypasses Traefik, expect reviewer friction). Required when another service in another region declares `links:` to this service.

expose_host_ack.description: Required acknowledgement for `ports.expose: host`. A host-published port is DNAT'd in PREROUTING and never reaches the nftables `input` chain, so it is never seen by the CrowdSec bouncer. `bin/bay validate` fails on `expose: host` unless this flag is true. Setting it changes nothing about the rendered port binding — it records a reviewed acceptance of the bypass.

secret.description: Secret environment variables — list of key names or key-to-vault mapping.

source_path.description: In-container path the `file` method backs up (docker cp source; also the restore target). Defaults to /data.

paths.description: Reserved for future use — not currently read by any backup method. The `file` method takes its in-container path from `source_path`, a separate key.

accessory.description: Name of the database accessory to bind to.

log_rotation.description: Per-container docker log retention. Either `false` (opt out, inherit daemon log-opts) or a partial override of log_rotation_defaults.

max_file.description: Number of rotated log files to retain.

log_retention.description: Opt-in host-side log archival with time-based retention. Archives land under /opt/<stack>/logs/services/<svc>/ and survive container recreation. Orthogonal to `log_rotation`; both can coexist on one container. Requires a compatible docker log driver (json-file or local).

days.description: Archive retention window in days. Daily rotation writes YYYY-MM-DD.log.gz; files older than this are alerted and pruned at 00:00 UTC.

max_total_size.description: Hard ceiling on the archive directory size (e.g. '500m', '2g'). Sum across host validated at deploy time against log_retention_budget_fraction * log_retention_disk_bytes.

mode.description: 'normal' (default): 0640, group-readable by the app-owner's log group. 'sensitive': 0600 root:root — the app-owner's log group cannot read. Use 'sensitive' for services that log detailed PII.
